title: A frog acts as well without the brain regions of consciousness as with them

statements.text: Molecular changes in the brain cause the states of consciousness of animals, but nothing shows that those states cause the molecular changes behind movement. A frog with the parts of its brain tied to consciousness removed walks, hops and swims as well as an intact frog. If a frog has anything like volition, it is a concomitant of the brain changes that produce motion.

sources.quote: Is there any evidence that these states of consciousness may, conversely, cause those molecular changes which give rise to muscular motion? I see no such evidence.
The frog walks, hops, swims, and goes through his gymnastic performances quite as well without consciousness, and consequently without volition, as with it
